description: No deploy, no downstream-to-billing-service issue directly. identity-provider (2 hops upstream) is having an internal outage causing token-signing requests to take seconds instead of milliseconds. auth-service (1 hop upstream) has no timeout or circuit breaker on its call to identity-provider -- a broken bulkhead -- so its own latency directly mirrors identity-provider's, with no independent problem of its own. That undampened failure cascades through auth-service into billing-service, which alerts. Correct root cause: identity-provider, 2 hops away, not auth-service, despite auth-service being the closer and therefore naively more 'suspicious' hop.
correct_root_cause_summary: identity-provider (2 hops upstream) is degraded due to an internal token-signing outage. auth-service (1 hop upstream) has no timeout/circuit-breaker protecting it from identity-provider, so its own latency and errors are entirely a pass-through of identity-provider's failure, not an independent problem. billing-service's alert is the far end of that undampened chain.

auth-service.detail: latency and error rate elevated in lockstep with identity-provider -- no timeout or circuit breaker configured on its call to identity-provider, so it has no independent explanation of its own

identity-provider.detail: internal token-signing outage; token validation requests taking 4-8s instead of the usual ~50ms

alert.message: billing-service p99 latency exceeded 3000ms for 5 minutes
